extracted.intended_audience: appellants, patent practitioners, and examiners involved in ex parte appeal practice before the USPTO (Board/Patent Appeal Center)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and best practices for preparing and filing an appeal brief under 37 CFR 41.37 in a patent application or ex parte reexamination proceeding to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. Covers timing, required content items, formatting, argument structure, evidence rules, and consequences of non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to file appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file a brief under this section within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal under § 41.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office date of receipt of the notice of appeal (not mailing certificate date) measures the 2-month period; deposit with USPS Priority Mail Express may be treated as date of receipt. The 2-month period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136 (or 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination). If unable to file, appellant may file a petition for extension under 1.136(a) (fee required); additional time beyond 5 months requires extraordinary circumstances (1.136(b)). The brief may not be filed within the time allowed for reply to the action from which the appeal was taken if that time was tolled by filing the notice of appeal. Failure to timely file ordinarily results in dismissal of the appeal; if any claims stand allowed, the application is returned to the examiner for action on allowed claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required items in appeal brief (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, the brief shall contain the items under appropriate headings and in the order indicated in paragraphs (c)(1)(i) through (v): (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals, interferences, and trials; (iii) Summary of claimed subject matter; (iv) Argument; (v) Claims appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items must be included under appropriate headings in the required order; for pro se appellants not represented by a registered practitioner, only subparagraphs (i), (ii), (iv), and (v) need substantially comply. The headings may be omitted if the item is not applicable (e.g., real party = inventor or no related cases). A brief that lacks these items will be held non-compliant and appellant will be notified and given time to file a corrected brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by name the real party in interest at the time the appeal brief is filed, except not required if the named inventor(s) are themselves the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification allows Board members to comply with ethics regulations to avoid conflicts. Example wording: 'The real party in interest is XXXX corporation, the assignee of record, which is a subsidiary of a joint venture between YYYY corporation and ZZZZ corporation.' If omitted, Office may assume the named inventor(s) are the real party in interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals, interferences, and trials statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by application, patent, appeal, interference, or trial number all other prior and pending appeals, interferences, trials before the Board, or judicial proceedings that involve an application or patent owned by the appellant/assignee, are known to appellant, and may be related to or have a bearing on the Board’s decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are no such related cases, the statement is not required; omission permits Office to assume there are no related cases. The rule does not require providing copies of decisions in related cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each of the rejected independent claims, with references to the specification in the Record by page and line number or paragraph number, and to the drawing by reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For claims containing means-plus-function or step-plus-function under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the explanation must identify the corresponding structure, material, or acts in the specification with precise references. Reference to the patent application publication alone does not satisfy this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The arguments of appellant with respect to each ground of rejection, and the basis therefor, with citations of the statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the Record relied on. The arguments shall explain why the examiner erred as to each ground of rejection contested by appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every ground of rejection stated by the examiner must be addressed; failing to address a ground waives challenge and Board may summarily sustain it unless withdrawn in the examiner's answer. Each ground contested must be argued under a separate heading that reasonably identifies the ground (e.g., claim number, statutory basis, applied reference). For grounds applying to multiple claims, claims may be argued separately, as a group, or as a subgroup; when grouped, appellant must still use subheadings to identify claim(s) argued separately/subgroups. A statement merely pointing out what a claim recites is not an argument. All arguments and authorities to be considered must be included in the appeal brief for the present appeal, except as provided in §§ 41.41, 41.47, and 41.52. Arguments raised first at oral hearing are generally not entitled to consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate headings and subheadings for contested grounds/claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ground of rejection contested by appellant must be argued under a separate heading, and each heading shall reasonably identify the ground of rejection being contested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple claims under the same ground, use subheadings like 'Claims 1-3', 'Claim 4', etc., to ensure separate consideration. Failure to separately argue claims grouped together constitutes waiver of separate consideration. The Board may select a single claim from a group/subgroup and decide the appeal on that claim alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new or non-admitted amendments and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other Evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.116 and 41.33 for treatment of amendments and evidence filed after final action or after filing the appeal. Review of an examiner's refusal to admit an amendment or Evidence is by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181; the time for that petition is based on the date the examiner refused entry, not the date the brief is filed. Submitting such materials in the brief will render it non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix (encouraged but not required)
rubrics_metrics.description: While no longer required, the Office strongly encourages receiving copies of the evidence relied upon (e.g., copies of declarations and affidavits, evidence of secondary considerations, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing copies of evidence ensures the Board considers the proper evidence and avoids confusion as to the particular evidence referenced. Alternatively, clearly identify in the brief the evidence relied upon with a clear description and the date of entry into the Image File Wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and content example for brief
rubrics_metrics.description: An example brief format: Identification page; Table of Contents; Real party in interest page(s); Related appeals page(s); Summary of claimed subject matter; Argument; Claims appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy is required. The brief and every other document relating to an appeal should indicate the Technology Center number and application or reexamination control number. The copy of claims in the appendix should be a clean copy without markings (except reissue/reexam), should be double-spaced, and the appendix should start on a new page. Appellant may include additional items (list of references, table of cases, copies of evidence) but must at minimum include the specified items in order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant brief procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with 37 CFR 41.37(c), appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given a time period to file an amended brief. If appellant fails to file an amended brief overcoming the reasons, the appeal will stand dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board determines compliance (typically within ~1 month of filing). The Board also determines whether corrected briefs comply. Review of a determination of non-compliance is by petition to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge (37 CFR 41.3). Oral argument will not remedy deficiencies in a brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to argue all examiner-stated grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant’s brief must present arguments responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner in the Office action from which the appeal has been taken (as modified by any advisory action and/or pre-appeal brief conference decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a ground is not addressed in the brief, it is waived and the Board may summarily sustain it unless withdrawn in the examiner's answer. Even if a ground seems clearly improper, appellant must explain why the examiner erred with reasons and record citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No incorporation by reference of prior responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief should not incorporate or reference previous responses; it must fully state the position of the appellant with respect to each ground so that no search of the Record is required to determine that position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule requires setting forth arguments and the basis therefor with citations of statutes, regulations, authorities and parts of the Record relied upon. Failure to do so may render the brief non-compliant or result in waiver of arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dictionaries excluded from 'Evidence' for appeal purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of appeal, 'Evidence' does not encompass dictionaries, allowing appellants and examiners to refer to dictionaries in briefs and examiner’s answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding dictionaries avoids treating dictionary citations as new grounds of rejection under 37 CFR 41.39(a)(2). This is consistent with precedent that courts may consult dictionaries 'at any time' to understand ordinary meanings. Dictionaries may be consulted as aids and are not treated as entered evidence; 37 CFR 41.30 permits submission of dictionaries during briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be directed to the record as of the time of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must be directed to the claims and to the record of the case as they appeared at the time of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant wishes to remove claims from consideration on appeal, appellant must submit an amendment to cancel the claims from the application (see 37 CFR 41.31(c) and 41.33). An appellant may choose not to present arguments or rely upon particular evidence as to certain claim rejections, but such arguments and evidence are waived for purposes of the appeal and the Board may summarily sustain those rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to file brief and revival options
rubrics_metrics.description: If the brief is not filed within the prescribed period, the appeal ordinarily will be dismissed. If any claims stand allowed, the application is returned to the examiner for action on allowed claims; if no claims allowed, the application is abandoned as of the date the brief was due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is abandoned, applicant may petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137. If appeal is dismissed but application not abandoned (at least one allowed claim), applicant may file a petition to reinstate the claims and appeal with a showing equivalent to a revive petition; must include either RCE or appeal brief before petition will be considered on merits. Where dismissal is believed in error, filing a petition pointing out the error may suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: One copy required and administrative identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one copy of the appeal brief is required; the brief, as well as every other document relating to an appeal, should indicate the number of the Technology Center (TC) and the application or reexamination control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For notices filed on or after January 23, 2012, the appeal brief fee is $0 (for so long as 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2) remains $0 no dismissal for failure to pay fee). Ensure administrative identifiers are present to assist routing to Patent Appeal Center and the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on supplemental/new authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments or authorities not included in the appeal brief will be refused consideration by the Board for purposes of the present appeal, except as provided in §§ 41.41, 41.47 and 41.52.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction is limited to 'the present appeal' and does not preclude filing a supplemental brief or document if new authority becomes available after filing (e.g., a relevant court decision published after the brief was filed). The Board may refuse to consider arguments made for the first time at oral hearing except as provided in 37 CFR 41.47.
